newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - YPF busy on quiet day.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - YPF busy on quiet day.

text.p: YPF SA's American Depositary Receipts were lifted to a new year-high in vigorous New York Stock Exchange trade on Monday after Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock and forecast higher crude oil and natural gas prices.
At midsession, the ADRs of YPF, an Argentine integrated oil and gas company, were up 3/4 to 24-5/8, easing slightly off the new peak of 24-3/4 notched earlier in the day.
Traders said YPF was the only ADR making notable moves in a market becalmed ahead of Christmas.

"The market is pretty dull with the exception of YPF. It was recommended by Morgan this morning, which is having an impact. We are looking for related followthrough on Transportadora de Gas del Sur SA and Metrogas SA," said a Bankers Trust trader.
Transportadora de Gas ADRs were unchanged at 12 and Metrogas ADRs gained 3/8 to 9-1/4, both on the NYSE.
Transportadora de Gas is an Argentine natural gas company with a 4,100 mile pipeline system, the largest in South America and Metrogas is an Argentine natural gas distribution utility.

Early Monday, Morgan said it raised its 1997 estimate on West Texas Intermediate crude to $20 per barrel from $18.50 and its estimate on natural gas for next year to $2.25 per thousand cubic feet (MCF) from $2.
Morgan also raised YPF to outperform from neutral.
At midday, almost one million YPF shares were traded, more than the stock's average daily volume of about 830,000 shares.
